To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TrwB is a DNA-binding protein that binds ATP tightly but is not a hydrolase and is required for R388 conjugative DNA processing.
the ATP binding activity of the conjugative coupling proteins is not essential for the function of the protein, but it is essential for the function in the plasmid.

(i) TrwB is a conjugative coupling protein; (ii) the soluble TrwB domain binds ATP tightly but lacks ATPase activity; (iii) TrwB binds DNA nonspecifically, and this binding enhances conjugative DNA processing; (iv) TrwB ATP-binding activity is essential for conjugation, and (v) TrwB has potential functions as a trigger of conjugative DNA-processing and as a molecular motor in the transport process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the ATP- and DNA-binding properties of TrwC, a conjugative coupling protein.
the molecular mechanism of bacterial conjugation, a process by which bacteria can share genetic material.
the characterization of the conjugative coupling proteins TrwB and TrwL of the IncW plasmid R 388.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TrwB is an ATP-dependent DNA translocase.
TrwB is an ATPase that binds to DNA and that the DNA binding activity is essential for conjugation, but that the ATPase activity is not.
ATP binding and ATP hydrolysis by TrwB is not essential for the transfer of plasmid DNA, although it may be important for other functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ATP binding site in TrwB is not required for its functions in conjugation.
TrwBΔC70 is a soluble protein with ATPase activity that is essential for R388 transfer, and TrwBΔS70 is a soluble DNA binding protein that stimulates nic cleavage.
TrwB is a coupling protein that is involved in DNA processing and transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TrwB is an ATPase that interacts with DNA and that this interaction enhances the cleavage of the nic site of the conjugative relaxosome.
the ATP binding activity of TrwB is not essential for conjugation.
the ATPase activity of TrwB is not essential for conjugative DNA processing, although it may be important for DNA transport.
